chunks: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله borrowed seventy smashing coats of mail from Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah al-Jumaḥī, and that was before his Islam. So he said, “Is it seizure or a loan, O Abā al-Qāsim?” He صلى الله عليه وآله said, “No, rather, it is a loan that will be returned.”

Thus the sunnah (prophetic tradition) came to be regarding a borrowed item, when it is stipulated in it that it be returned. And Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah, after his Islam, was sleeping in the mosque, and his cloak was stolen. So he followed the thief and took the cloak from him, and brought him to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and established against him two just witnesses. So he عليه السلام ordered that his right hand be cut off.

Then Ṣafwān said, “O Messenger of Allah, will you cut him off because of my cloak? I have gifted it to him.” He عليه السلام said, “If only this had been before you brought him to me.” So he cut him off. Thus the sunnah (prophetic tradition) came to be regarding the hadd: when it is raised to the Imam and the proof is established against him, it is not to be suspended, and it is to be carried out.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: The normative prophetic precedent established by this incident.
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: The lawful authority before whom the case is brought.
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: The clear legal evidence by which the case is proven.
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: The mosque, where the theft incident occurred.
key_terms.شَاهِدَيْنِ عَدْلَيْنِ: Two upright witnesses establishing legal proof.
key_terms.عَارِيَّةٌ: A borrowed item given for temporary use.
key_terms.مُؤَدَّاةٌ: Required to be returned to its owner.

ai.seo_question: When can a borrowed item or a hadd punishment no longer be waived in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This report establishes two legal precedents through the practice of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله: that a borrowed item must be returned when stipulated, and that a hadd punishment is not to be waived once the matter reaches the Imam and the legal proof is established. It also preserves an incident involving Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah that illustrates both property rights and judicial procedure.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4086 - The Prophet (may Allah (swt) bless him and his family) borrowed seventy coats of mail made of iron from Safwan ibn Umayyah al-Jumahi before he embraced Islam.
Safwan asked: "O Abu al-Qasim, is this a seizure or a loan?"
The Prophet (may Allah (swt) bless him and his family) replied: "No, it is a loan to be returned."

Thus, it became a precedent that a loan (ariyyah) must be returned if stipulated.
After Safwan embraced Islam, he was once sleeping in the mosque when his cloak was stolen. Safwan pursued the thief, retrieved the cloak, and brought him to the Messenger of Allah (swt) (may Allah (swt) bless him and his family). He also presented two just witnesses against the thief.
The Prophet (may Allah (swt) bless him and his family) ordered that the thief's right hand be cut off.

Safwan said: "O Messenger of Allah (swt), will you cut off his hand because of my cloak? I have already gifted it to him."
The Prophet (may Allah (swt) bless him and his family) said: "Why did you not say this before bringing the matter to me?"
The sentence was then carried out, establishing the precedent that if a case reaches the Imam and evidence is presented, the prescribed punishment (hadd) cannot be waived.
